name: Armour Traits
gist: Traits give armour advantages or disadvantages; (X) is a rating, replaced by a number
text: Some pieces of armour have Traits that give them advantages or disadvantages over others. Some of the Traits listed below have (X) in their name, representing a rating. The pieces of armour with this Trait will have a number instead of ‘X’ which is used for any calculations.

name: Invulnerable
gist: Armour Rating marked *; AP does not affect your Resilience
text: Any Armour Rating marked with an asterisk (*) is Invulnerable. If you are wearing Invulnerable Armour, AP does not affect your Resilience.

name: Bulk (X)
text:
Heavy and restrictive armour possesses the Bulk trait.

Bulk reduces the Speed of the wearer by a number of metres equal to its rating.

name: Cumbersome
text:
Large suits of armour can severely restrict movement.

You cannot Run or Sprint in Cumbersome armour.

name: ’Ere We Go!
gist: Ork wearer ignores Bulk and Cumbersome when Wounded
text:
The latent psychic power of an Ork empowers their armour, allowing them to fight harder when harmed.

An Ork wearing armour with this Trait ignores the Bulk and Cumbersome Traits when Wounded.

name: Power Field
gist: Roll Determination against attacks that deal Mortal Wounds
text:
Wonders of archeotech, personal Power Fields envelope their user in a protective barrier of energy.

Armour with this Trait allows you to roll Determination against attacks that deal Mortal Wounds.

name: Powered (X)
gist: +X Strength; not knocked Prone on a Complication firing an unsecured Heavy weapon
text:
This armour is designed to augment the wearer’s might through the marvels of mechanisation.

Whilst wearing armour with this Trait you gain a Strength bonus equal to the rating. Additionally, you are not knocked Prone when you roll a Complication while firing an unsecured Heavy weapon.

name: Shield
gist: Add AR to Defence and Resilience, if the GM agrees you can manoeuvre it to block
text:
Wielded like a defensive weapon, shields are carried instead of worn, and used to deflect incoming attacks.

Armour with this Trait adds its AR to your Defence and Resilience, provided the GM agrees you can manoeuvre the shield to block the attack.

name: Agile
gist: The wearer may use Agility instead of Toughness to calculate Determination
text: A few types of armour listed in this section have the Agile trait. A character wearing Agile armour may use their Agility to calculate their Determination instead of their Toughness.

name: Void
gist: Incoming attacks' AP is reduced one step (AP −1 to 0); also counts as Built-in Tech (Core p.235)
text:
A number of types of armour listed in this section have the Void trait. A character with Void armour reduces the AP of incoming attacks by one step (i.e., from AP -1 to 0, or from AP -3 to -2).

Void armour also benefits from the Built-in Tech rule (page 235 of the Wrath & Glory Core Rulebook).
